prompt.context: Our client is an online dating startup named Grad-U-Date, which specializes in matching graduate students with other graduate students. Grad-U-Date has finished building their website and are now looking for your assistance in deciding on a strategy to monetize their website.
prompt.question: What is Grad-U-Date's best method of monetization? How profitable will the company be?

clarifying_info.q: What is the gender ratio of users?
Which types of graduate students are in scope?
clarifying_info.a: MBA, law, and medical students are considered professional students. Non-professional graduate students are also in scope.

clarifying_info.q: Has the website already been built?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the website has already been built and is considered a sunk cost.
Grad-U-Date will only operate within the United States.
There are 4 major competitors and hundreds of small competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any recent market trends to be aware of?
clarifying_info.a: There has been a significant increase in the number of free dating phone apps starting in late 2012.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other dating services focused on graduate students?
clarifying_info.a: There are currently no other online dating services that focus only on graduate students.

clarifying_info.q: Can Grad-U-Date use multiple revenue models simultaneously?
clarifying_info.a: Only one revenue model can be used.

exhibits.title: Student Enrolment Information
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of new graduate students per university per year by student type, and the number of years for each degree program.

data.note: There are currently 1,000 universities in the United States and all universities have all four groups of students.

exhibits.title: Product Usage
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of forecasted percentage of graduate students using Grad-U-Date under each revenue model, plus pricing details for each model.

Premium Account model.premium_uptake: 40% of men and 25% of women purchase premium accounts

framework: Market size: estimate the total addressable population of graduate students in the US
Competitive landscape: assess major and minor competitors and market share dynamics
Monetization model brainstorm: identify all viable revenue models and their pros/cons
Target market analysis: evaluate whether to restrict to a segment (e.g. MBA-only) or serve all grad students
Profitability calculation: for each candidate revenue model, compute revenue minus fixed and variable costs
Revenue model recommendation: select the model with the highest sustainable profit, considering market trends
Risk assessment and next steps: identify risks to the chosen model and actions to mitigate them

questions.prompt: Monetization Brainstorm: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use, and what are the advantages and disadvantages of each?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate at least 3 models. Strong candidates reach 5+. Expected models include: Monthly Fee (predictable revenue, but limits user base), Advertising (free to users, maximizes reach, ad revenue depends on engagement), Pay for Premium Account (freemium model, balances reach and revenue), Profile Consulting Services (high margin, niche upsell), Micro-Transactions (e.g. pay per message, pay for profile bump — flexible, low barrier), Pay per Message, Pay for bump in profile traffic.

questions.prompt: Target Market Brainstorm: Grad-U-Date is considering limiting the site to only MBA students. What issues might there be with an MBA-only dating website?
questions.guidance: Key issues: (1) Gender skew — more men than women at most MBA programs. (2) Unnecessarily limits market size. (3) MBA students tend to be older, so many are already married or in committed relationships.

questions.prompt: Market Sizing: What is the potential market size for Grad-U-Date? (Share Exhibit 1 with candidate)
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 data and multiply enrolled students per university by 1,000 universities. Steps: compute steady-state enrollment per university (new per year x years in program), sum across types, multiply by 1,000 universities.

math.setup: Steady-state enrollment per university = new students per year x years in degree. Total market = students per university x 1,000 universities.

questions.prompt: Revenue Model Calculation: Calculate the profit of each revenue model. Fixed costs are $10,000,000 per year and variable operating cost is $1 per member per year. Which revenue model would you recommend? (Share Exhibit 2 with candidate)
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute revenue and profit for all three models and recommend the one with highest profit. Monthly Fee has highest profit at $25.7M.

math.setup: Profit = Revenue - Fixed Costs - Variable Costs. Variable Costs = number of users x $1. Fixed Costs = $10,000,000.
math.answer: Monthly Fee: $25.7M profit; Premium Account: $23.3M profit; Advertising: $16.2M profit. Based on raw calculation, Monthly Fee yields highest profit.

questions.prompt: Additional Q1: Does the information in Exhibit 3 change your recommendation for which revenue model? (Share Exhibit 3 with candidate)
questions.guidance: Candidate should switch recommendation from Monthly Fee to Premium Account. Exhibit 3 shows that both the percentage of users paying a monthly fee and the average monthly fee paid have been rapidly decreasing since 2008 (accelerating after 2013). It is unlikely current Monthly Fee profitability will be maintained. Premium Account is more resilient.

questions.prompt: Additional Q2: Why do you think the percentage of users paying monthly fees dropped so quickly starting in 2013?
questions.guidance: Key reasons: (1) Increased competition in the online dating market. (2) Quality free dating apps released that are more convenient. (3) Tinder launched in late 2012, dramatically disrupting willingness to pay for monthly fee models.

questions.prompt: Additional Q3: Given your recommended revenue model (Premium Account), what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should bucket answers into cost reduction and revenue increase. Reduce Costs: outsource servers; provide only email support (no phone). Increase Revenue: create a mobile app to attract more customers; offer profile consulting services; profile photo editing; deals with popular date locations; expand to recent graduate school alumni; add micro-transactions (e.g. pay to boost profile visibility); incorporate social media.

recommendation: Grad-U-Date should adopt the Premium Account revenue model

The Monthly Fee model should not be selected because the share of users willing to pay a monthly fee and the average fee paid have been rapidly decreasing due to competitive pressure from free apps (notably Tinder, launched late 2012)
The Premium Account model is expected to generate approximately $23.3M in annual profit
risks: Premium account adoption could be seeing a similar decline in share as the monthly fee model
A smaller percentage of users than forecasted may purchase premium accounts
The ad-supported model could be growing faster than the premium account model
Graduate students may not be able to afford premium accounts
The number of people enrolling in graduate school could decrease
Graduate students may prefer not to limit their dating pool to other grad students
next_steps: Explore building a mobile app to attract more users
Research market trends for ad-supported and premium account revenue models to validate assumptions
Expand into adjacent markets such as undergraduates or international markets
Offer additional services: profile consulting and date-location deals
Add micro-transactions (e.g. paying to increase profile traffic)
Evaluate whether premium account and advertising models can be combined
Incorporate social media integrations to drive user acquisition
